user_summary_md:
## Your Situation

You are 38 with an existing balanced portfolio. Your goal is portfolio improvement with a 5-10 year horizon. Current allocation: 60% equity, 30% bonds, 10% cash — well-structured for your risk profile.
portfolio_diagnosis_md: Portfolio is moderately diversified. Concentration risk is at moderate levels — some rebalancing may improve risk-adjusted returns. Cost drag is a consideration if you are holding high-expense-ratio active funds.

options.title: Risk Reduction — Shift Defensive
options.best_for: Investors wanting to reduce portfolio volatility
options.content_md:
### Asset Allocation
| Asset | Allocation |
|---|---|
| Equity | 45% |
| Bonds | 40% |
| Cash | 15% |

### Why this works
Reduces equity beta while maintaining some growth.

### Pros
- Lower volatility
- More stable returns

### Cons
- Lower long-term expected returns

### Agent guidance
Consider if approaching major liquidity event within 3-5 years.

options.title: Gradual Rebalance to Low-Cost Index
options.best_for: Investors with active funds who want to reduce costs without disrupting allocation
options.content_md:
### Asset Allocation
| Asset | Allocation |
|---|---|
| Low-cost index funds | 70% |
| Bond ETFs | 20% |
| Cash | 10% |

### Why this works
Swap active funds for index equivalents. Reduces expense drag significantly.

### Pros
- Reduces cost drag
- Maintains diversification

### Cons
- May trigger tax events on switch

### Agent guidance
Prioritise switching highest-cost funds first.

options.title: Goal-Aligned Growth Tilt
options.best_for: Investors with 10+ year horizon comfortable with higher equity
options.content_md:
### Asset Allocation
| Asset | Allocation |
|---|---|
| Equity index | 80% |
| Bonds | 15% |
| Cash | 5% |

### Why this works
Higher equity weight maximises long-term returns for a 10yr+ horizon.

### Pros
- Higher expected return
- Low cost if using index funds

### Cons
- Higher short-term volatility

### Agent guidance
Suitable only if you won't need the money for 10+ years.

hidden_disclosures: Active mutual fund expense ratios typically 1-2%/yr — check your fund fact sheets.
Switching between funds may trigger capital gains tax events.
Bond funds may have minor exit loads on early redemption.
STCG applies if equity sold within 12 months of purchase.
